conflicts.point: Whether frontier training runs exceeding 10^26 FLOPs generate emergent, unmanageable risks that justify mandatory pre-deployment interpretability gates and compute-indexed regulatory oversight.

positions.stance: Frontier models exceeding 10^26 FLOPs produce irreversible capabilities that require mandatory pre-deployment safety verification and compute-indexed oversight.
Compute thresholds and interpretability metrics cannot reliably capture emergent continuous optimization dynamics, making such mandates an ineffective regulatory barrier.
Pre-market verification requirements for probabilistic model weights are empirically intractable and function primarily as anti-competitive moats.

verdicts.conflict: Whether frontier training runs exceeding 10^26 FLOPs generate emergent, unmanageable risks that justify mandatory pre-deployment interpretability gates and compute-indexed regulatory oversight.
verdicts.rationale: Safety advocates highlight systemic risks from unmanaged scaling, but accelerationists correctly identify that rigid thirty-percent mandates ignore multi-year energy procurement timelines. Skeptics add that National Institute of Standards and Technology licensing creates compliance moats that favor large incumbents over smaller labs. The debate remains deadlocked because neither side provides empirical data proving whether mandatory budget reallocations prevent catastrophic failures or simply stall market competition.
